messages.content: Can you find me any upcoming rock and jazz concerts for the next month in San Francisco, California and New York, New York?

function.name: concert_finder
function.description: Locate upcoming concerts based on music genre in specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state to find concerts.

time_period.description: Number of days to search upcoming concerts.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function twice: one for San Francisco, CA, and one for New York, NY. The function signature: concert_finder(location: string, music_genre: string, time_period?: number). We can pass location "San Francisco, California" or "New York, New York". For each, we want upcoming concerts for the next month (default 30 days). So we call with location and music_genre. But the user wants both rock and jazz concerts. We could either call twice per location: one for rock, one for jazz. Or we could combine? The function expects a single music_genre. So we need to call twice per location. That means total 4 calls. But maybe we can combine into one call per location if we pass multiple genres? The function only accepts a string for music_genre. So we can't pass multiple. So we need separate calls.

Thus we will call concert_finder for San Francisco, CA with music_genre "rock", then again with "jazz". Then same for New York, NY. We'll use default time_period=30.

We'll produce calls accordingly.
